newsitem.title: USA: Iowa issues local phone arbitration decision.
newsitem.headline: Iowa issues local phone arbitration decision.

text.p: Iowa phone regulators said Friday they issued a proposed settlement covering the terms and conditions under which AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp will hook up to U S West Media Group local phone network in the state.
The regulators said the proposed agreement is one of the first arbitration decisions in the nation between a local phone company and its potential competitors.

The Iowa Utilities Board said the pact reflected the last, best offer proposed by AT&T for the two long-distance companies to "interconnect" with U S West as part of their efforts to break into the local phone market.
It did not provide details. An AT&T spokesman was not immediately available to comment on the details of his company's offer.
The agreement outlines the prices, terms and conditions under which AT&T and MCI will connect with U S West's network and facilities.
The arbitration process was spelled out under the recent telecommunications law enacted by Congress earlier this year.

The companies have 10 days to provide comments on the board's agreement. The board will then issue a final decision requiring the companies to submit specific agreements consistent with the board's order.
